chapters.1.lds: What human costs do the repeated charges name?
chapters.1.summary: Amos is a herdsman from Tekoa in Judah. He speaks in the days of King Jeroboam of Israel. The LORD roars from Zion, and the pastures wither. Amos announces judgment on the nations around Israel. Damascus threshed Gilead with iron sledges. Gaza and Tyre sold whole communities to Edom. Edom chased his brother with a sword and showed no pity. Ammon ripped open pregnant women to gain more land.
chapters.2.lds: Why do garments and wine beside altars expose wrongdoing?
chapters.2.summary: Amos continues with Moab, which burned the bones of Edom’s king. Then he turns to Judah, which rejected the LORD’s law. Last he turns to Israel itself. The people sell the innocent for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals. They trample the heads of the poor. They lie down beside altars on clothes taken as security for debts. They told the prophets not to speak. God will press them down like a loaded cart.
chapters.3.lds: The 2026 lesson connects prophetic speech with receiving God’s instruction. Why does chosen belonging increase responsibility?
chapters.3.summary: God speaks to the whole family he brought up from Egypt. He chose them alone of all the families of the earth. Therefore he will punish them for their sins. Amos asks a series of questions about cause and effect. A lion does not roar without prey. When the LORD speaks, a prophet must prophesy. Foreign peoples are called to witness the oppression in Samaria. The rich houses of winter and summer will be destroyed.
chapters.4.lds: The lesson invites return to God during trials. It does not claim that God sends every personal trial. What remains unchanged throughout the repeated disasters?
chapters.4.summary: Amos speaks to the wealthy women of Samaria who crush the poor. They will be led away with hooks. He tells the people, with irony, to go and sin at their shrines. They love to bring offerings and announce them. God sent hunger, drought, blight, plague, and ruin. After each one they did not return to him. So Israel must prepare to meet its God. He forms the mountains and creates the wind.
chapters.5.lds: The lesson studies seeking God and choosing good as a path toward life. How do unfair courts explain the rejection of festivals?
chapters.5.summary: Amos sings a funeral song for Israel. God tells the people to seek him and live. They turn justice into bitterness and hate anyone who speaks truth in court. They tax the poor and take bribes. They should hate evil and set up justice at the gate. The day of the LORD will be darkness and not light. God says he hates their feasts and will not hear their songs. He wants justice to roll like a river.
chapters.6.lds: What suffering do the comfortable leaders refuse to grieve?
chapters.6.summary: Amos warns those who feel safe in Zion and Samaria. They are the leading men of the first of the nations. They lie on beds of ivory and eat choice lambs. They sing to the harp and drink wine by the bowlful. They do not grieve over the ruin of their people. So they will be the first to go into exile. God hates Jacob’s pride and will give up the city. They have turned justice into poison.
chapters.7.lds: The lesson studies Amos’s calling as an example of God speaking through prophets. Why does Amaziah call Bethel the king’s sanctuary?
chapters.7.summary: God shows Amos a swarm of locusts and then a fire. Each time Amos pleads, and God relents. Then God shows him a plumb line set among the people. He will spare them no longer. Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, reports Amos to the king. He tells Amos to go home to Judah and earn his bread there. Amos answers that he was a herdsman and tended fig trees. The LORD took him from the flock and sent him.
chapters.8.lds: The lesson applies hunger for God’s words to spiritual life. It also connects this image with the later Apostasy and Restoration. How do false measures connect trade with loss of freedom?
chapters.8.summary: God shows Amos a basket of ripe summer fruit. The end has come for Israel. Amos speaks to those who trample the needy. They ask when the holy day will be over so they can sell grain. They shrink the measure, raise the price, and use false scales. They buy the poor for silver and sell the sweepings as wheat. God swears he will not forget. A famine is coming, a hunger to hear the LORD’s words.
chapters.9.lds: How do inhabited cities reverse earlier warnings about lost houses?
chapters.9.summary: Amos sees the Lord standing beside the altar. He orders the temple struck, and no one will escape. Israel is no different to him than distant peoples. He brought the Philistines and Syrians from other lands too. He will sift Israel like grain and not destroy it completely. Then he will raise up David’s fallen shelter. The people will rebuild their ruined cities and live in them. They will never again be uprooted from their land.
